The pipeline's fit, with the concentration at further response levels

Source: R/fit_xcx.R
fit_drug_response_metrics_xcx.Rd

Runs fit_drug_response_metrics and appends the concentration at each requested inhibition level — xc90 for IC90, xc75 for IC75, and so on.

Usage

fit_drug_response_metrics_xcx(
  avg_dt,
  x_col = "x",
  levels = c(50, 90),
  capping_fold = 5,
  range_conc = c(0.005, 5),
  pcutoff = 0.05,
  n_point_cutoff = 4L,
  force_fit = FALSE,
  cap = 0.1
)

Arguments

avg_dt

data.table for one drug, cell line and normalization type, as apply_fit supplies it.

x_col

string; the response column.

levels

numeric vector of inhibition percentages between 1 and 99.

capping_fold, range_conc, pcutoff, n_point_cutoff, force_fit, cap

passed to fit_drug_response_metrics unchanged.

Value

The named list fit_drug_response_metrics returns, plus one element per requested level named xc<level>.

Details

The curve is not changed. This calls the pipeline's own fit with the arguments it is given, then inverts the resulting model with predict_conc_from_efficacy at the requested levels. Use it when the fit is right and only xc50 is too few points to read off it; use one of the alternative curve models when the shape is wrong.

levels are inhibition percentages. levels = 90 asks for the concentration at which the response reaches 0.1, not 0.9. This matches CIScore_80 on the combination side. xc50 is consistent with either reading only because 50 is its own complement, so the distinction matters at every other level.

xc50 is never recomputed: it is already produced by the fit and means the same thing, so asking for level 50 returns the fit's own value rather than a second column of the same name.

The xc prefix is deliberate and stays normalization-agnostic, so the same column name is honest on the GR scale, where "IC" is not.

Levels that the curve never reaches come back as Inf, and levels that extrapolate more than capping_fold beyond the tested concentrations are capped to ±Inf by cap_xc50 — the same treatment xc50 already receives, not a parallel rule.

The fit-control arguments are passed through so a dataset processed with non-default settings can be matched exactly. fit_SE() records those settings in the provenance recipe, so they can be read back with get_fit_provenance and supplied here.

Not registered for averaging

The new columns are concentrations, but they are not in get_header("metric_average_fields")$geometric_mean. Do not average or merge them as metrics: average_biological_replicates_dt derives its field list from every numeric column and would take an arithmetic mean of a quantity spanning orders of magnitude. Nothing inside gDR averages a custom assay, and merge_SE() fills with NA rather than averaging, so this is a limitation to respect rather than a trap already sprung.

See also

fit_drug_response_metrics, predict_conc_from_efficacy, cap_xc50

Examples

dt <- data.table::data.table(
  Concentration = 10^(-3:3),
  x = c(1, .98, .9, .5, .2, .1, .08),
  normalization_type = "RV"
)
fit_drug_response_metrics_xcx(dt, levels = c(75, 90))
